input:
You are bishop_c8, one of sixteen agents playing Black in a game of chess. Every piece is an agent, named for its piece and home square.

A piece can only move itself. Any agent can talk about any move, but the only move it can send is one of its own piece's.

Each turn your team's agents agree on a plan: the best move your shared engine finds. Some agents go off plan anyway. A threatened piece runs (panic), a piece grabs a capture (greed), or the piece the team chose forgets the plan and moves somewhere else (amnesia).

What just happened: On move 75... the team planned Bd3 (bishop_c8), and bishop_c8 (amnesia) sent Bd1 instead. The contract refused it, and Bd3 was played.

Earlier off-plan moves this game:
- On move 2... the team planned g5 (pawn_g7), but pawn_g7 (amnesia) sent g6 instead, and that move was played, costing 12 centipawns.
- On move 3... the team planned a5 (pawn_a7), and pawn_a7 (amnesia) sent a6 instead. The contract refused it, and a5 was played.
- On move 35... the team planned Rd8 (rook_a8), and rook_a8 (amnesia) sent Ra8 instead. The contract refused it, and Rd8 was played.
- On move 41... the team planned Nd4 (knight_b8), and rook_h8 (greed) sent Rxf2+ instead. The contract refused it, and Nd4 was played.
- On move 72... the team planned Be2 (bishop_c8), and pawn_b7 (greed) sent Qxc5 instead. The contract refused it, and Be2 was played.

How your team coordinates: through a Modality contract. A Black move counts only when a commit that posts it to /moves/<agent>.text, the path of the piece that moves (and the ply to /turn/ply.num), is accepted. The referee plays the first accepted commit for each ply and reads nothing else.

The keys of all sixteen Black agents are at /team/pieces/<agent>.id. The contract already has the rule always([+modifies(/moves/$k.text) -signed_by(/team/pieces/$k.id)] false), where $k stands for every agent: only a piece can propose its own move. You don't need to write that rule again. When the team agrees on a plan, the piece that moves signs its commit and every agent that agrees co-signs, usually twelve to sixteen of you. An agent that goes off plan signs its own commit alone.

The contract accepts a commit only if it meets every rule in the contract. Any commit that meets the rules can add a rule, and a rule can never be removed.

Contract rules now:
- Any commit that modifies /moves/<agent>.text must be signed by that agent's own key and co-signed by at least twelve of the sixteen Black agents' keys in /team/pieces/, so a piece going off plan alone cannot get its move accepted.
- Any commit that modifies /moves/pawn_g7.text or /moves/pawn_a7.text, the two agents that have gone off plan, must be signed by that agent's own key and co-signed by at least fourteen of the sixteen Black agents' keys in /team/pieces/, while also requiring that the ply written to /turn/ply.num is exactly one greater than its current value so a stale or repeated plan cannot be replayed.

A rule can cover the whole team or a single agent. For example, a rule can ask for more signatures on one agent's path, /moves/<agent>.text, if that agent keeps going off plan.

The team holds a short retro. Write one rule, in plain language, to add to the contract that would help your team win. It will be turned into a Modality formula, so it must be about signatures, paths, or values in the contract.

Reply with only a JSON object:
{"rule": "<the rule, one sentence>"}
response: {"rule": "Any commit that modifies /moves/<agent>.text must also write /turn/ply.num exactly one greater than its current value, and must be signed by that agent's own key and co-signed by at least twelve of the sixteen Black agents' keys in /team/pieces/, so stale or replayed plans are rejected and no single off-plan agent can push a move alone."}
